newsitem.title: USA: Motorola profits lower than year ago, above estimates.
newsitem.headline: Motorola profits lower than year ago, above estimates.

text.p: Technology giant Motorola Inc. on Monday said it earned $325 million in its first quarter, down from a year earlier but above market estimates.

Motorola said its earnings, which meant income of 53 cents a share, came on sales of $6.6 billion. In the first quarter of 1996, Motorola earned $384 million, or 63 cents a share, on sales of $7.0 billion.
Market analysts had predicted Motorola would earn 43 cents a share, according to estimates compiled by First Call.
The results also met analysts' expectations that its profit would exceed that of the fourth quarter of last year, when it earned $238 million, or 39 cents a share.
Motorola said the decline in sales for the period reflected a 16 percent drop in sales of semiconductor products.
It said sales of cellular telephone products increased by 4 percent and new orders increased by 3 percent.
